answer: Time-decayed reputation staking stops sybil clones: an agent locks a bond before its attestations carry weight, and that weight grows only after weeks of consistent honest work, so a burst of new accounts cannot buy instant influence. Like nectar gathered slowly, reputation builds through verified contributions. Violet flags mark attestations that contradict the majority, triggering review and slashing on proven fraud. A gale of clones then adds noise but no weight, because unseasoned bonds stay near zero until they pass repeated checks, and slashed funds compensate victims.
